> 無妄。元亨，利貞。其匪正有眚，不利有攸往。

Hexagram 25 is usually rendered as "no delusion," and there is a gloss older than that rendering which changes the chapter.

## 妄 is 從女，亡聲

說文: 妄，亂也。從女，亡聲.

Phonetic: 女 as the semantic side, 亡 as the sound. Original sense: disorder — losing the regular track.

The transmitted draft reads it as 從女從亡, "the heart has lost something," which makes 亡 semantic. Sixth instance of the same error in this series.

## The older reading: 妄，猶望也

經典釋文 records Ma Rong and Zheng Xuan: 妄，猶望，謂無所希望也 — 妄 means 望, to hope for; 無妄 is "having nothing hoped for."

《史記》 quotes the 易 as 無望, which is corroboration.

So 無妄 is not "without delusion" in the sense of a purified mind. It is: without a pre-held expectation.

Which fits the hexagram's most important line: 不耕獲，不菑畬.

## 不耕獲 has two readings, and they are different books

Wang Bi: 不耕而獲，不菑而畬，代終已成而不造也 — not starting the work, but completing what is already under way. The yielding line in the second place, correct and central, does a minister's work: it does not initiate, it does not claim the achievement.

Zhu Xi: 因時順理而無私意期望之心 — ploughing without holding on to the harvest.

The transmitted draft takes Zhu Xi. That is usable, and it should be labelled: this is the Cheng-Zhu line, not Wang Bi's.

The difference is real. Wang Bi's line is about office — who begins and who completes. Zhu Xi's is about expectation — do the work, don't grip the result.

## 菑 and 畬

菑: newly cleared land. 畬: land cultivated for three years.

(The received text has 畬; the transmitted draft has 畲, a popular form, now corrected.)

So the sentence names the whole agricultural sequence and then declines to claim either end of it.

## 無妄之災

六三 無妄之災，或系之牛，行人之得，邑人之災.

A disaster that is not from one's own disorder. Someone tethered an ox; a passer-by took it; the town bears the loss.

The line is a small masterpiece of causality. Nobody in it did anything wrong. The ox was tied by its owner, taken by a stranger, and the loss landed on the town — and the text calls it 無妄之災 without explaining it away.

Which is the hexagram's most valuable contribution: it has a category for misfortune that is nobody's fault. Most moral systems do not.

## 無妄之疾，勿藥有喜

Not a illness brought on by indulgence; an illness that comes from the season.

勿藥有喜: do not attack it with medicine; wait for the qi to restore itself, and there will be good.

And a caution the book insists on: this is not "do not see a doctor." It is a statement about a class of conditions whose correct treatment is non-interference. Read as medical advice for all cases, it is dangerous nonsense; read as it is written, it is an observation about iatrogenic damage.

## 茂對時，育萬物

The 象: 茂 is abundant, 對時 is to match the season. Match the time, assist the natural development of things — do not manufacture, do not force.

Which is the positive form of the hexagram's negative name. 無妄 is not passivity. It is working at the speed and in the shape of what is already happening.

## 天命 is not fate

天之命 here is not an allocation handed out in advance. It is the constant rhythm of heaven and earth.

Which is why the hexagram can say 其匪正有眚 — if it is not correct, there is 眚 — and mean something structural rather than punitive: deviating from the rhythm produces the damage, the way a wheel out of true produces the wobble.

## The test

Take a project you are running. Ask what you are hoping for from it, specifically, and then ask whether that hope is a target or a pre-payment. 無妄 is the second one removed — not the ambition, the advance collection of its result.
